pmsims 1.1.0: A learning-curve search engine

Source: vignettes/release-1-1-0.Rmd
release-1-1-0.Rmd

pmsims 1.1.0 introduces a new learning-curve search engine, which is now the default.

A new search engine

In 1.0.0, the search had two stages: an adaptive search for start values, followed by a Gaussian-process search using the mlpwr package. In 1.1.0 the default is a learning-curve engine, method = "curve":

  • Every replicate is kept, and a monotone learning curve, \(C(n) = a - b n^{-c}\), is fitted to the criterion (e.g. the 20th percentile of the calibration slope) at each sample size simulated so far.
  • A pilot doubles or halves \(n\) from a heuristic start until the criterion has been seen on both sides of the target. Each further batch of replicates is placed where the fitted curve crosses the target.
  • The minimum sample size is where the final curve crosses the target. It is a median-unbiased estimate, reported with a bootstrap interval (diagnostics$curve$n_ci) and a shape-free cross-check (diagnostics$crosscheck_n).

The previous engine is still available with method = "mlpwr".

Seeing the search

plot() shows the criterion at each simulated sample size, the fitted learning curve, the target, and the minimum sample size with its interval. With live_plot = TRUE, the plot is redrawn after each batch of replicates during the search. The getting-started vignette shows an example.

The cores argument runs the replicates in each batch in parallel (on Unix-like systems). Each replicate has its own random-number stream, so results are reproducible with set.seed() and are the same for any number of cores.

Checking the result

Every result now has a status. The minimum sample size is simulated again with fresh replicates (verify_reps, default 100), and results that fall clearly below the target are flagged:

status Meaning
"ok" A sample size was found, and simulating it again confirmed the target is met
"not_verified" Simulating the minimum sample size again gave performance clearly below the target
"not_bracketed" No sample size up to max_n met the target
"unreachable" The learning curve levels off below the target (curve engine only)
"replicates_failed" Too many replicates failed to fit or score the model

When no sample size is found, min_n is NA and status_message explains why. For an unreachable target, the message says what performance is achievable.

Corrections

Several corrections were made to the simulation, so sample sizes may differ from those given by 1.0.0. These include:

  • Correlated predictors now have the requested pairwise correlation.
  • Replicates whose metric is not finite count as failed replicates.
  • Metrics where smaller is better ("calibration_in_the_large", "brier_score", "ibs") can no longer be used as search targets.
  • The concordance fallback in survival_auc has been corrected.

Speed

Calibration slopes, AUC, concordance, linear predictors and correlated predictors are all faster to compute, with unchanged results. A binary glm search takes about two thirds of the time it did, and a Cox search about a quarter.

Upgrading from 1.0.0

  • To use the previous search engine, set method = "mlpwr".
  • min_n and perf_n are NA when no sample size is found (they were a character message). Check status and status_message.
  • The simulate_*() wrappers no longer suppress warnings. A result whose status is not "ok" raises a warning with its status_message.
  • metric_2_at_n is now the mean over 10 replicates at min_n (it was a single replicate).
  • Custom metric functions without a "metric" attribute count failed replicates as 0.5, with a message. Set attr(metric_function, "value_on_error") to choose another value.
  • With method = "mlpwr", n_reps_total is raised to 2000 for "lm", "glm" and "coxph" models with at most 10 signal parameters. A message says so, and auto_n_reps_total = FALSE keeps the value supplied.

The changelog lists every change.

Install 

install.packages("pmsims")

The overview paper by Shamsutdinova et al. (2026) and the validation paper by Olaniran et al. (2026) describe the package and its validation.
